newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet fuel under supply pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet fuel under supply pressure.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel market, which has enjoyed a rally over the past three weeks, was set to succumb to increase supplies due to shipments from the West and higher output at regional refineries, traders said on Tuesday.
A US trader offered prompt jet fuel at $24.20 for July 15-19 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis, 40 cents below Monday's offers, which traders said could push prices lower.
But the US trader also offered a July 17-21 parcel at $24.65, while a Chinese trader offered at five cents over that for the same date range.

Traders noted that buyers were sidelined in anticipation of lower jet values as two cargoes were said to be fixed to Asia for end-July delivery from the Mediterranean, while refiners in Singapore have maximised output since last week.

Traders also said that cracks have started to be seen as swaps jet/gas oil regrade slipped to $1.90/$2.05 per barrel, down 10-15 cents from Monday. The regrade for foreard months were even narrower woth August at $1.55/$1.70, down 25 cents.
Gas oil was also thinly discussed with buyers at bay despite offers being lowered by 10 cents to $22.30 mid-half July lifting fob, and another offer at $165 per tonne ($22.15 per barrel).
Traders said a reported deal at a discount of 75 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, fob could have been done some time ago between a European major and an Asian trader for mid-July lifting.
Traders said regional supplies remained abundant while emerging demand from China was not enough to absorb the glut.
But prices were steady largely due to strong crude values.
More supplies are expected to emerge from South Korea, which would be the main source for China, as well as from Japan along with the start of a liberalised export market.
